text:
The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered - Switch 2 vs PC Graphics Comparison
The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered finally makes its way to the Switch 2. And just like the 2025 version, Oblivion remastered brings everything old people like me loved about the original game to a new generation of consoles with vastly improved graphics, gameplay, and a ton of other quality of life features. The Switcha 2 port makes that even better by allowing you to play the game on the go
While the Switch 2 port isn’t the prettiest version of the game because it’s a handheld. It holds up surprisingly well when compared to a PC running a an RTX 5090 and its console counterparts.
On the switch 2 you’ll get the game running at a pretty stable 30fps in both docked and handheld modes with Handheld outputting the game at 900p and docked hitting 1080p thanks to DLSS. That being said it's lowest point is the long load times. In our testing we were seeing some load screens last over 20 seconds on the Switch 2. 
Regardless, The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered is a great way to play a classic RPG on the go. 
 
Gameplay captured on a docked Nintendo Switch 2 and a PC with an RTX 5090 GPU with the settings cranked all the way up.

text:
Coyote vs. Acme Review
Coyote vs. Acme has had a long and strange road to the big screen. Once buried by Warner Bros. for tax reasons, brought back to life by popular outcry, the story of Wile E. Coyote suing the heartless Acme corporation for decades of faulty products is ready to hit theaters. Starring Will Forte, John Cena, Lana Condor and a cast of Looney Tunes that doesn't seem to leave many animated favorites out, Coyote vs. Acme wound up being the perfect answer to the real world corporate shenanigans it survived.

IGN's Clint Gage reviews to talk about the importance of side characters, balancing genuine emotion with pantless modeling gigs and the Batman and Joker dynamic at the heart of this movie.
